findings.cross_file_justification: The gate is implemented as three per-method overrides (complete, validate_config, health_check) on a subclass of HeadlessCLIAdapter (headless_cli.py, not in diff). Any other base-class entry point that spawns the CLI, or any future base method, dispatches agy with the prompt on argv while the operator believes the route is off. The TypeScript planner (bridgebuilder multi-model-pipeline.ts, truncated) evaluates the same key independently, so two readers can disagree.
findings.description: The cycle-127 opt-in is enforced inside individual adapter methods rather than at the single construction/registry seam (get_adapter / provider registration). The subclass only guards the three methods it happens to override; the base HeadlessCLIAdapter surface (and anything added to it later) is unguarded. The test suite monkeypatches agy_opt_in_enabled in three separate test modules to keep the opted-in path alive, which shows how spread-out the enforcement is.
findings.failure_mode: A base-class method that reaches the CLI (or a new one added later), or a planner that constructs the adapter and calls something other than complete(), spawns `agy -p <prompt>` while hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in is false. The untrusted review prompt lands in /proc/<pid>/cmdline on a shared host exactly as before the gate existed, and the one-time WARN that documents the exposure is never emitted because that WARN sits inside complete().
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce the gate once at the factory seam: have get_adapter (or AgyHeadlessAdapter.__init__) raise AgyOptInRequiredError, or refuse to register the gemini-headless class, when the opt-in is off. Keep the per-method checks as belt-and-braces but add a contract test that iterates every public method of HeadlessCLIAdapter and asserts none spawns a process while the gate is off.

findings.cross_file_justification: agy_headless_adapter.complete() calls agy_opt_in_enabled() with no project_root, so the decision is made from the cheval process cwd at dispatch time. The adapter's own module docstring states the caller's cwd is the reviewed tree. cmd_invoke in cheval.py already resolves the project root and config once and could pass the decision down.
findings.description: The opt-in is re-read from disk on every hop via a cwd walk (_find_project_root) and merged over load_system_defaults. The docstring promises 'a planner is never talked into the agy voice by ambient env', but cwd is itself ambient: a `.loa.config.yaml` in the reviewed tree or any ancestor directory, or a `headless.agy_opt_in: true` in the system defaults layer, flips the gate without any operator action in the invoking project. `_find_project_root()` is also evaluated outside the try/except, so an exception there propagates as a raw error rather than the fail-closed False.
findings.failure_mode: The review pipeline runs with cwd inside a checkout that carries its own `.loa.config.yaml` (for example a PR branch or a vendored subproject) with agy_opt_in: true. The agy route is enabled for that run and the redacted diff is placed on argv, readable by every local account, while the operator's own config says the route is off.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the opt-in once in cmd_invoke from the already-resolved project root and plumb it into ProviderConfig (or the adapter constructor) instead of walking cwd per hop. Log the file path the value was read from at INFO on first use. Move `_find_project_root()` inside the try so a failure there also reads as off.

findings.description: resolve_effort is documented as the single chokepoint for effort, and it validates the catalog and extra rungs against _EFFORT_LEVELS, but the caller rung returns `explicit` unvalidated on the assumption that argparse already checked it. The value then flows into CompletionRequest.effort, the MODELINV audit envelope, and (via build_headless_argv) a `--effort <value>` argv pair handed to the Claude CLI. Any programmatic caller that builds an argparse.Namespace directly, or a future flag that relaxes choices, bypasses validation at the one place that claims to own it.
findings.failure_mode: An unexpected string reaches the CLI as `--effort <string>` and the audit log. Because it is a single argv element there is no shell injection, but an out-of-set value can produce CLI usage errors that walk the fallback chain, and the telemetry schema's effort field receives arbitrary content.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `explicit` through _valid_effort too and WARN-and-ignore (or raise INVALID_CONFIG) on mismatch, so the chokepoint validates every rung regardless of origin.

findings.description: The new shared builder accepts a `prompt` parameter that, when non-None, places the prompt directly on argv after `-p`. The adapter currently passes None (stdin transport, the cycle-126 fix that closed the /proc/<pid>/cmdline exposure), but the builder is now a public module-level function shared with tools/ceiling-probe-live.py and reintroduces the argv-prompt surface as a one-argument choice.
findings.failure_mode: A future caller passes `prompt=<review content>` to build_headless_argv, and the untrusted diff becomes readable by every local user through `ps` and /proc for the life of the hop. The adapter's own docstring treats this exposure as the reason the agy route needed an opt-in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `prompt` parameter from the builder (the adapter and the probe both use stdin), or have ClaudeHeadlessAdapter._build_command assert `prompt is None` and add a contract test asserting no argv element exceeds a small length, mirroring the probe test's `all(len(a) < 1000 for a in argv)` check.

findings.cross_file_justification: The writer under test is tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:write_catalog_operator_set (truncated from the diff). The tests assert byte-identical prefixes and suffixes around the edited entry (bl[:start] == al[:start]), which shows the catalog is edited by text splicing rather than a YAML dump, and that cli_version, cli_model and host_route are interpolated into both a comment line and ceiling_calibration fields.
findings.description: write_catalog_operator_set splices operator-supplied strings (--cli-model, --host-route) and the CLI binary's `--version` stdout (cli_version) into the routing catalog as YAML scalar values and into reprobe_trigger. The catalog is the file that drives model routing and input ceilings and is paired with a checksum. Nothing in the visible tests rejects a value containing a newline, `: `, or `#`. The ceiling itself is type-checked (ValueError on 0, -1, True, '500000'), so the gap is only the string fields.
findings.failure_mode: A wrapper binary on CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (the Bedrock wrapper pattern the tests model) emits a multi-line or colon-bearing `--version`, or an operator passes a crafted --host-route. The spliced text yields a catalog that either fails to parse (loader falls back to defaults silently or loudly) or gains an unintended key inside the claude-opus-5-5 entry, altering routing for every subsequent invoke.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate cli_version, cli_model and host_route against a conservative regex (printable, single line, no `:`/`#`) before splicing, quote them as YAML strings, and re-parse the result with yaml.safe_load plus the ceilingCalibration schema inside the tool before writing. Refuse to write if the round-trip changes anything other than the target entry.
